yt.description:
Same $100,000 salary, ten provinces, and a $6,506-a-year gap between the top and the bottom. Here's how much you actually keep in 2026.

Take-home after federal and provincial income tax, CPP/QPP and EI (+QPIP in Québec), single, employment income only:
B.C. $75,373 · Alberta $74,459 · Ontario $74,206 · Saskatchewan $72,288 · Manitoba $71,445 · New Brunswick $71,215 · Newfoundland & Labrador $70,603 · P.E.I. $69,789 · Nova Scotia $68,867 · Québec ≈ $69,585 (separate Québec return, estimate).

Why B.C. beats Alberta at this salary: B.C.'s first two rates (5.6% and 7.7%) are lower than Alberta's (8% and 10%).

Sources: CRA T4127 (2026), 2026 provincial budgets, Revenu Québec. Estimates; general information, not tax advice.

$100K in Canada: how much do you actually keep? It depends on one thing: your province. 🇨🇦

B.C. $75,373 → Nova Scotia $68,867. That's $6,506 a year, $542 a month, on the same salary (2026, single, after income tax, CPP/QPP and EI). And no, Alberta isn't #1 at this salary.

Save this if you're thinking about moving provinces, and send it to the friend who always says 'Alberta has the lowest taxes'.

research:
- vidIQ keyword research (CA, 2026-10-05): '100k salary after tax canada' <750/mo (long tail); head terms 'tax brackets canada' ≈3,458, 'income tax canada' ≈4,728, 'how taxes work in canada' ≈4,908, 'taxes in canada' ≈3,485, 'canadian taxes' ≈3,954, 'tax return canada' ≈4,573 (low competition 10.6).
- vidIQ IG/TikTok outliers: '$100K SALARY How much do you keep?' (a Canada-vs-US comparison reel) at 79× its creator's median confirms the hook; 'moving provinces / is anywhere worth it in Canada' and 'Canadians leaving' are active discussions. No creator content is copied; our angle is the 10-province ranking with a verified calculation.
- vidIQ title scores: 'Same $100K, 10 Provinces: Who Keeps the Most?' 81; '$100K Salary After Tax in Every Province (2026)' 75; 'Why B.C. Beats Alberta on a $100K Salary (2026)' 85. The highest scorer gives away the #1 reveal, so it is used as alternative A/B, not primary, to protect the open loop.
retention: Hook: a $100K card plus the question ✅. Open loop: 'one leaves you thousands more' ✅ (who wins is held to 32 s). Density: the bottom and middle ranks are grouped in the VO for pace; the screen shows exact numbers ✅. Change rate: a card every 1–4 s ✅. Escalation: bottom → middle → top 3 → twist ✅. Reveal: #1 B.C. after a dramatic pause ✅. Payoff: the gap $6,506/yr = $542/mo ✅. CTA ✅. Fixed during production: an empty frame at every card change (v1); cards double-exposed in the fast sequence (v3).
